key_insight: CuAD transforms CUDA kernels into tangent and adjoint CUDA code, enabling accurate discrete-adjoint sensitivities for GPU-based flow solvers.
engineering_relevance: GPU-native derivatives support aerodynamic shape optimization and data assimilation while avoiding finite-difference Jacobian errors.
method: Generate tangent and adjoint kernels through source-to-source automatic differentiation.
Organize reverse mode by GPU thread, recomputing intermediates and differentiating pure accumulations without a tape.
Assume non-aliasing inputs and outputs; store any remaining tape in fixed thread-local arrays.
evidence_signal: Across four flow-model kernels and a 2D Euler solver, derivatives passed dot-product tests to round-off, adjoint kernels cost 2–6× the primal, and transonic NACA 0012 adjoint sensitivities agreed with tangents to 10⁻¹³.
watch_item: Application requires respecting the non-aliasing convention and checking fixed thread-local tape requirements for each kernel.
paper_title: CuAD: Source-to-Source Automatic Differentiation of CUDA Kernels for Discrete Adjoints in Computational Fluid Dynamics
